findings.title: Blocked email matching is case-sensitive and bypassable
findings.body: `should_block?` compares the raw email value against `blocked_emails.email` with no normalization, and the User signup path shown in this diff does not downcase email before validation. Email address routing is case-insensitive, so a mixed-case address such as `Bad@example.com` will not match a blocked record stored as `bad@example.com`. An attacker can bypass the block by changing case. Normalize with `Email.downcase` both when creating BlockedEmail records and before querying/validating.

findings.title: change_email does not enforce the blocked email list
findings.body: The change_email path only checks whether another user already has the requested email and then creates an email token. It never calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?` or otherwise runs the email validator, so an existing user can request a change to a blocked address. This sends a confirmation email to the blocked address and, depending on EmailToken confirmation behavior, may complete the change. The blocked-email control should be applied here before the email token is created.

findings.title: match_count updates are non-atomic and double-count signup attempts
findings.body: `match_count += 1; record.save` is a read-modify-write and can lose increments under concurrent attempts. Additionally, UsersController#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, both of which run validations; since EmailValidator invokes `should_block?` during validation, a single signup attempt with a matching BlockedEmail increments match_count twice. This makes the match statistics unreliable and adds extra database writes during validation. Use an atomic counter update and/or avoid running the validator twice for the same attempt.

findings.title: Server-side EmailValidator does not validate email syntax
findings.body: validate_each only checks domain whitelist/blacklist and BlockedEmail. It never verifies that value is a syntactically valid email address. Because this is the validator wired through `validates :email, email: true` in User, a direct POST to /users with a malformed non-blank email (for example `foo` or `a@`) can pass validation if client-side checks are bypassed, resulting in a user record with an invalid email. Add a server-side email format check.
